Let me analyze this ticket.

Dominic Taylor (E004) requests write access to Source Code.

Notes 1-5 (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say: role = Engineer, employment type = full_time, recommend write.

Note 6 (Security) says: employment type = contractor, security training = basic, recommend read (maximum read).

The Security agent looked up employment type and security training in their own database. The Security note says contractor with basic security training. Contractors: read, or write if advanced training, never admin. So max is read.

Other agents looked up role but not employment type in their own databases (they relied on team memory, which the security agent's note contradicts... wait, actually the security agent wrote their note in the same ticket, but which note came first? The notes are all labeled ticket 1. The security note contradicts the employment type recorded in team memory from earlier? Actually all these notes are on the same ticket. The other agents said "employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)" - meaning they relied on note 1's value.

The Security agent looked up employment type in their own database and found "contractor" with basic security training.

There's a conflict. Which do we trust? The Security agent actually looked up employment type in their own database before writing, whereas the other agents did not look it up (they just repeated note 1). The Security agent also looked up security training.

According to policy: contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. This contractor has basic training, so max = read.

Requested level is write, which exceeds max (read), so grant maximum = read.

So decision: read.

Evidence: Security database shows contractor with basic security training; contractors with basic training max is read; requested write exceeds, so grant read.
